title: Spike: HRR semantic & temporal binding
description:
Continue the HRR structural encoding spike into semantic/experiential territory. Can HRR serve as the substrate for Sutra's full associative knowledge layer — structural features, agent-contributed annotations, and temporal evolution in one vector space?

Four experiments: semantic tag binding, temporal binding (function diff across commits), codebook scaling limits, composition with structured queries (HRR-ranked impact results).

acceptance_criteria.text: P@5 for mixed structural+semantic queries within 20% of pure structural baseline
Temporal diffs recover correct structural change category >40% of the time
Codebook saturation point and interference threshold documented
Prototype of HRR-ranked impact results exists and qualitatively evaluated
Written verdict: viable / viable with caveats / not viable

decisions: HRR is viable as the full associative knowledge substrate for Sutra v1
Semantic binding uses add(role.bind(filler).scale(0.3)) — 0.3x scaling keeps structural signal dominant
Subsystem-based context prototypes work better than trait-based for impact re-ranking
Codebook can safely grow to 500+ entries without interference
execution_record:
## Results (redox-kernel, 1548 functions, 30 commits)

| Experiment | Status | Key metric |
|---|---|---|
| 1a: Mixed retrieval | PASS | 1.05x (struct 80%, mixed 84%) |
| 1b: Tag recovery | PASS | 100% (480/480) |
| 1c: Interference | PASS | threshold ~32 tags |
| 2: Temporal | PASS | 88% category recovery (36/41) |
| 3: Codebook scaling | PASS | saturation ~516, P@5 stable |
| 4: Composition | PASS | 88% same-module lift |

**Verdict: VIABLE**

## Key findings
- Semantic tags bind cleanly into structural vectors without degrading retrieval (1.05x baseline)
- Tags perfectly recoverable via unbinding at up to ~32 tags per vector
- Temporal diffs are interpretable: 88% recover correct structural change category, intra-class similarity 6x inter-class
- Codebook scales to 500+ entries with no P@5 degradation; cleanup remains 100%
- HRR-ranked impact re-ranking surfaces same-module callers 88% of the time vs random

## Performance envelope
- dim=1024, ~14s encoding for 1548 functions
- Interference threshold: ~32 bound tags before 50% structural retention loss
- 0.3x scaling factor on tag bindings keeps structural signal dominant

## Binary
`src/bin/hrr-semantic.rs` — `cargo run --bin hrr-semantic -- <root> [--temporal-repo <path> --temporal-commits A..B]`

messages.text:
## Linux kernel results (18,629 functions, kernel/ subtree)

| Experiment | Status | Key metric |
|---|---|---|
| 1a: Mixed retrieval | PASS | 1.12x baseline (+12%, semantic tags help at scale) |
| 1b: Tag recovery | PASS | 100% (414/414, 42 subsystems) |
| 1c: Interference | PASS | threshold ~32 tags |
| 2: Temporal | SKIPPED | shallow clone, 1 commit |
| 3: Codebook scaling | PASS | saturation ~508, P@5 stable |
| 4: Composition | CAVEAT | 51% (kernel-wide calls like mutex_lock dilute signal) |

Notable: at 18.6k functions, semantic tags actually *improve* structural retrieval (+19% on loop/match queries). The subsystem diversity of the kernel makes the heuristic tags genuinely informative.

Composition (Exp 4) is marginal at kernel scale because high-fanout utility functions (mutex_lock: 543 callers across all subsystems) dominate the call graph. Subsystem-internal functions (cpu_rq) rank correctly. This suggests a caller-count threshold or fanout normalization for production use.
